description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.focus: Check against the change's spec delta (openspec/changes/implement-platform-foundation-ui/specs/platform-foundation/spec.md) and the store specs gamification ('Light and dark theme') and content-authoring (CA-D21). Pay attention to: the lint rule's false negatives (literal text it misses), whether the pseudo-catalog test can pass while a string bypasses the catalog, the theme and a11y e2e actually iterating every route, the provenance check's coverage of fixture/asset roots, nginx proxying and SPA fallback, the Dockerfile build with the contract submodule, and tsconfig splits leaking Node types into app code.

findings.title: Literal value on a text input/textarea is missed by both the lint rule and the pseudo-catalog render
findings.evidence: For DOM elements, `value` only counts as text when `element === "input" && VISIBLE_VALUE_INPUT_TYPES.has(staticAttribute(opening, "type"))`. So `<input value="Tvoje odpověď" />`, `<input type="text" value="…">`, `<input type={kind} value="…">` (where `staticAttribute` returns null) and `<textarea value="…">` are all allowed, even though the browser shows that value in the field. The backstop doesn't catch it either: `uiTexts` in src/app/i18n-coverage.test.tsx:47 only reads `el.value` for submit/button/reset inputs, and a controlled value is not a DOM text node. A Czech literal can reach the screen with both NFR-9 checks passing.
findings.suggestion: In the rule, treat `value` on `<textarea>` as text, and on `<input>` unless the static type is a known non-text type (hidden, checkbox, radio, number, range, color, date…); a non-static type should count as text. In `uiTexts`, collect `.value` from HTMLTextAreaElement and from text-like inputs. Add RuleTester cases for both.

findings.title: Lint rule misses literals in method-call arguments, callbacks and createElement
findings.evidence: For a CallExpression with a member callee, `literalTexts` only looks at the receiver (`return literalTexts(node.callee.object)`). Any other call falls through to `default: return []`. So `{t('a').concat(' bodů')}`, `{t('x').replace('{n}', 'Ahoj')}`, `{items.map(() => 'Ahoj')}`, render props such as `render={() => 'Zavřít'}` and `createElement('p', null, 'Ahoj')` all pass. The header comment says the rule catches `t('a') + ' bodů'` and method calls on a literal, but these equivalent forms get through. The pseudo-catalog test is the only backstop, and it only sees the first render of each route.
findings.suggestion: For member calls, also walk the arguments (skip identifier-like args where needed). Follow ArrowFunctionExpression expression bodies and return statements in JSX children and text props. Treat `createElement`/`React.createElement` children args as text. Add invalid RuleTester cases for each form.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test only checks the first render of each route, so text in later states bypasses it
findings.evidence: `renderSettled` renders `<App messages={pseudo} />` and waits one macrotask (`setTimeout(resolve, 0)`). Loading, error, empty and post-interaction states are never rendered, and query results that arrive after that tick are never seen. The lint header and the spec delta both call this test the backstop for text 'reached through a variable or another module'. A literal held in a constant and shown only in an error or success state passes both checks. Today it makes no difference (there is only the shell), but the guarantee is weaker than the spec wording.
findings.suggestion: Either narrow the spec wording to 'initial render of every route', or let screens register extra states (fixtures or MSW handlers for loading, error and empty) that the test renders with the pseudo-catalog. Wait for queries to settle with `waitFor` or `queryClient.isFetching() === 0` instead of a single tick.

findings.title: 'No control switches the theme' e2e passes while activating zero controls
findings.evidence: Both current screens (shell and not-found) have no buttons or switches, so `activated` stays 0. The test only adds an annotation (`annotations.push({ type: 'controls activated', ... })`) and reports PASS. AGENTS.md's 'vacuous-pass-not-earned' lesson says a check whose evidence scope is 0 must not render as PASS. The comment hands coverage to theme-source.test.ts, but that is a regex source scan, not the 'No toggle' scenario the spec states.
findings.suggestion: When `activated === 0`, call `test.skip()` with a reason (shown as SKIP-pending), or assert `activated > 0` on screens declared to have controls (e.g. a `hasControls` flag in SCREENS). Then the qa battery never counts this scenario as PASS over nothing.

findings.title: Theme source scan misses class/style-based theme switches and non-TS files
findings.evidence: `THEME_WRITE = /data-theme|dataset\.theme|colorScheme|color-scheme/` only scans `.ts/.tsx/.css` under src. It does not scan index.html (e.g. `<meta name="color-scheme">` or an inline pre-paint theme script), `.js/.jsx` files, or theme switches via `classList.toggle('dark')` or a theme context. The e2e only runs on reachable states, so the source scan is the stated cover for the rest, and it misses these forms.
findings.suggestion: Also scan index.html and `.js/.jsx`. Consider matching `prefers-color-scheme` overrides and `classList.*(dark|light)`, or assert in e2e that `<html>` class and style are unchanged after the controls are clicked.

findings.title: Provenance scope misses TS/JS data modules and common archive and markup formats outside the fixture roots
findings.evidence: Outside FIXTURE_ROOTS and ASSET_ROOTS, a file is in scope only if it matches MEDIA, DOCUMENTS or `SOURCE_DATA = /^(src\/(?!design-system\/)|e2e\/).*\.(json|md|ya?ml)$/`. Workbook text or answer keys committed as `e2e/data/tasks.ts`, `src/features/task/__fixtures__/tasks.ts`, `*.html`, `*.xml`, `*.jsonl` or `*.zip` are never checked. NFR-4 forbids workbook text and answer keys anywhere, and TS data modules are the most likely form in this codebase.
findings.suggestion: Add `__fixtures__/`, `__mocks__/` and `e2e/data/` (any extension) as fixture roots, and add html/xml/jsonl/zip/tar/7z to DOCUMENTS. Alternatively, require every non-spec file under `e2e/` other than `*.spec.ts` to be listed.

findings.title: Docker docs/qa exemption accepts any string in any manifest.json, not just recording paths
findings.evidence: `recordedFiles` walks every string value in each `docs/qa/**/manifest.json` and adds both `dirOf(m)+v` and `v` to the exempt set. Any field (title, source, notes) that happens to equal a docs/qa path exempts that file, e.g. a PDF under docs/qa named in a 'source' field. The intent is to exempt only recordings the recorder wrote.
findings.suggestion: Read only the manifest's clip/recording path fields (per the recorder's schema), and require the exempt file to have a media extension (webm/mp4/png).

findings.title: a11y e2e ignores moderate axe violations, so missing landmarks and headings never fail
findings.evidence: `violations.filter((v) => v.impact === 'serious' || v.impact === 'critical')` drops everything else. Rules such as `heading-order`, `landmark-one-main`, `page-has-heading-one` and `region` are moderate, so a screen with no `<main>` or no h1 still passes. This matches the spec delta's wording, but NFR-13 says 'WCAG AA', and the dropped violations are not reported at all, not even as annotations.
findings.suggestion: Report moderate violations as test annotations or attach them to the QA report, so they are visible even if not failing. Consider failing on moderate violations too, once the shell is stable.

findings.title: SPA fallback returns index.html (200) for /api without trailing slash and for missing non-asset files
findings.evidence: `location /api/` only matches with a trailing slash, so a request to `/api` (or `/apix`) falls into `location / { try_files $uri /index.html; }` and gets the SPA HTML with 200. The same applies to `/favicon.ico` and `/robots.txt`. A client or health check that hits `/api` gets HTML instead of the backend's problem+json, which can hide misrouting.
findings.suggestion: Add `location = /api { return 404; }` or proxy `location /api` as well, and serve missing files that have an extension outside /assets/ as 404 (e.g. `location ~ \.[a-z0-9]+$ { try_files $uri =404; }`).

findings.title: Route matching uses exact pathname, so '/index.html' and trailing-slash variants show not-found
findings.evidence: `routes.find((r) => r.path === window.location.pathname)` compares strings exactly. Through nginx, `GET /index.html` serves the shell file but the pathname is '/index.html', so NotFound renders. Future paths such as '/admin/' vs '/admin' have the same problem. The pathname is also read during render with no popstate subscription, so back/forward navigation (once a second route exists) will not re-render.
findings.suggestion: Normalise the pathname (strip a trailing slash, map '/index.html' to '/'), or adopt the router now. If the interim approach stays, subscribe to popstate.

findings.title: nginx answers any Host header, so DNS rebinding exposes the unauthenticated child API to any website
findings.evidence: The only server block has no server_name allowlist and no default_server that rejects unknown hosts. Line 53 also forwards the client's $http_host to the backend unchanged. Attack: a site the child (or anyone on the LAN) visits rebinds its own domain to the stack's address, e.g. 127.0.0.1:8081 (the smoke-test port in tasks.md 4.4) or the LAN IP. Its scripts then make same-origin requests through this proxy to the /api/child/* endpoints, which need no login. They can read the display name (child PII, NFR-3) and progress, and submit attempts. That breaks the LAN-only intent of NFR-2. The admin surface is safe because its SameSite=Strict cookie belongs to the real host.
findings.suggestion: Add `server_name` with the expected hosts (localhost, 127.0.0.1, the LAN IP/hostname, maybe from an env template). Add a separate `default_server` block that returns 444 or 421 for any other Host. Or validate Host/Origin in the backend. Add a container-config test that requests with a foreign Host are rejected.

findings.title: 51 MB request bodies are allowed on every /api/ path, including the unauthenticated child endpoints
findings.evidence: `client_max_body_size 51m` is set for the whole server. NFR-17 only needs 50 MB on admin uploads, and the comment says child bodies are capped at 16 KB by the backend. Any LAN device (or a rebinding page, see the Host finding) can send repeated 51 MB POSTs to /api/child/*. nginx accepts and buffers each one, often to disk, before the backend rejects it. That is cheap disk and bandwidth exhaustion on the home server.
findings.suggestion: Set a small server-wide default (e.g. `client_max_body_size 64k`). Raise it to 51m only in a dedicated `location /api/admin/` block (or the specific upload paths). Assert the split in src/test/container-config.test.ts.

findings.title: Lint rule and pseudo-catalog backstop both miss `value` on text inputs and textareas
findings.evidence: The lint rule reports `value` only on <input type=submit|button|reset> (line 112). The render backstop reads input values only for those same types (src/app/i18n-coverage.test.tsx:173). `<input readOnly value="Odpověď" />`, `<input value="Doučko">` (no type, so text) and `<textarea value="…">` all put visible Czech text on screen. They pass both checks: the pseudo-catalog test goes green while a string bypasses the catalog. CSS `content:` strings in app or feature CSS are also outside both checks (app.css is clean today).
findings.suggestion: In the rule, treat `value` as text on <input> unless the static type is hidden, checkbox, radio, number, range, color, date or similar, and treat `value` on <textarea> as text. In uiTexts(), push `.value` for every HTMLInputElement/HTMLTextAreaElement whose type shows text. Add RuleTester and coverage cases for both.

findings.title: Provenance check misses workbook content stored as TS/JS modules or in uncovered formats
findings.evidence: Outside fixtures/, e2e/fixtures/ and evals/cases/, data counts only if it is .json/.md/.yaml under src/ or e2e/ (SOURCE_DATA). Media and documents count only by the listed extensions. A contributor can commit transcribed workbook tasks and answer keys as `src/features/task/__fixtures__/tasks.ts`, `e2e/data/tasks.ts` or `fixtures-like` .html/.xml/.zip files, and the check passes. That is the NFR-4 / CA-D21 breach it is meant to stop. Also, recordedFiles() (line 82) exempts any string that appears anywhere in any docs/qa/**/manifest.json. A workbook PDF at docs/qa/x.pdf is exempt as soon as some manifest value names it.
findings.suggestion: Treat any `__fixtures__/`, `fixtures/` or `data/` directory segment anywhere in the tree as a fixture root, whatever the extension. Add html/xml/zip/7z/tar/gz/svgz to the media/document sets. Limit the recording exemption to the manifest's clip/screenshot fields and to media extensions.

findings.title: Review coverage note: areas checked clean; dependency audit not executed
findings.evidence:
Checked clean in this diff:
- (1) Authz: no endpoints or API calls are added; the generated client is unused so far.
- (2) Sessions: no auth code in this slice.
- (3) Injection: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or HTML sinks; the CSP has script-src 'self' and no inline script in index.html.
- (4) Exposure: no CORS settings in the frontend; same origin via nginx; X-Forwarded-For is overwritten, not appended (line 56 of nginx.conf).
- (5) Privacy: e2e uses the fictional 'Agent Nova', and the real-name guard never prints the name.
- (6) Secrets: no VITE_* variables; .env/.env.* are gitignored and dockerignored; npm ci --ignore-scripts; base images pinned by digest.
- tsconfig split: app code has `types: ["vite/client"]`, and tests and src/test are excluded, so Node types do not leak into app code.
- e2e routes: a11y and theme e2e iterate ROUTE_PATHS plus not-found.
- SPA fallback: /assets/ misses return 404; the shell is served with `expires -1`, and the server-level add_header still applies.
- Contract submodule: the Docker build fails if contract/api/openapi.yaml is missing.
Not executed: `npm audit` was denied permission in this run, so dependency advisories for react 19.3, react-query 5.104, openapi-fetch 0.17 and vite 8.3 were not checked. Backend compose port bindings (../backend/compose.yaml) could not be read.
findings.suggestion: Run `npm audit --omit=dev` (and the full audit for build-time tools) and attach the output to the slice evidence. Have the backend review confirm the compose `ports:` for the frontend bind to 127.0.0.1 or the LAN interface, not 0.0.0.0. Confirm the backend port is not also published, which would let clients bypass the X-Forwarded-For overwrite.

findings.title: Coverage summary: 16 scenarios: 10 implemented, 6 partial, 0 missing, 0 contradicted
findings.evidence: Implemented: Dark OS, Light OS, Literal text is a lint error (every listed example is in the RuleTester invalid set), Reduced motion, Smoke in three browsers, Unlisted asset fails, Licensed asset without its licence, Real name on a page, Guard not configured against a stack, Every contract path is generated. Partial: No toggle (passes with zero controls), Pseudo-catalog render (known bypasses), axe on every route (the recorded run does not include the not-found screen), Image build without the contract (only a static check), API through the frontend origin (only a static check, live smoke 4.4 not done), Missing asset (only a static check).
findings.suggestion: Handle the major findings below. Then re-run qa:verify and the compose smoke so that every scenario has executed evidence.

findings.title: Lint rule misses literal text returned from callbacks and passed as call arguments
findings.evidence: Spec: 'A lint rule SHALL refuse literal UI text that it can see in `src/` (JSX, props, nested collections, the document title)'. In `literalTexts`, ArrowFunctionExpression and FunctionExpression fall to `default: return []`. The CallExpression branch only inspects the receiver of a member call (`literalTexts(node.callee.object)`) or the arguments of `String(...)`. So these patterns, all visible in a JSX child or prop, are not reported: `{items.map(() => 'Ahoj')}`, `<Tip render={() => 'Ahoj'} />`, `{(() => 'Ahoj')()}`, `{fmt('Ahoj')}`, `{t('x').replace('{n}', 'Ahoj')}`. I could not lint a probe file because the command was denied, so this judgment comes from reading the code.
findings.suggestion: Recurse into the body of an arrow or function expression (expression body and ReturnStatement arguments) when it is a JSX child or a component prop. Also inspect the arguments of member and identifier calls. Add these cases to the invalid set in src/test/lint-rule.test.ts.

findings.title: Document-title lint check only matches the bare `document.title`
findings.evidence: Spec: the lint rule covers 'the document title'. `isTitle` requires `left.object.type === 'Identifier' && left.object.name === 'document'`, so `window.document.title = 'Doučko'` and `globalThis.document.title = …` are not reported. DOM writes such as `el.textContent = 'Ahoj'` and `el.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Zavřít')` are also not seen. The pseudo-catalog test catches the title at render time, but the lint rule is required to catch it as well.
findings.suggestion: Match any MemberExpression chain that ends in `document.title`. Also consider reporting literal assignments to `textContent`/`innerText` and `setAttribute(<text attr>, literal)`.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test can pass while a string bypasses the catalog
findings.evidence: Scenario: 'every visible text node, text attribute and the document title consists only of whole ⟦…⟧ segments'. Gaps in `uiTexts`: (1) TEXT_ATTRIBUTES has no `value`, and only submit/button/reset input values are read, so a text input or `<input defaultValue={x}>` whose literal comes from a variable or another module (which the lint rule cannot see) passes both checks. (2) `renderSettled` waits one macrotask and reads the initial state only, so strings shown in loading, error or empty states, after a query resolves, or after interaction are never rendered. (3) Text from CSS `content:` is not read. (4) The not-found test has no `texts.length > 1` guard, unlike the route test, so an empty render passes.
findings.suggestion: Read `value` for every input and textarea, and add the length guard to the not-found case. Document in the spec that coverage is limited to the initial state, or have each slice add a state matrix (loading/error/empty) to the pseudo-catalog test.

findings.title: Recorded e2e evidence covers only '/', not the not-found screen the spec requires
findings.evidence: The spec says '"Any route" includes the not-found screen' (theme) and 'Every route, and the not-found screen, SHALL have no serious or critical axe-core … violation' (a11y). e2e/screens.ts now adds `{ name: 'not found', path: '/no-such-screen' }`, but the run quoted as evidence for task 4.1 ('npm run qa:verify green') shows 'Running 33 tests'. The only theme and a11y titles in it are '/ uses the light theme', 'axe, dark › / has no serious…', and so on. No 'not found' test was run, so the not-found coverage has no evidence and the ticked 4.1 is stale.
findings.suggestion: Re-run `npm run qa:verify` and refresh automated-verification-latest.md. The run should show 'not found' theme, axe and reduced-motion tests in all three projects. Untick 4.1 until that is done.

findings.title: 'No toggle' e2e passes without activating any control; the static backstop has gaps
findings.evidence: Scenario: 'WHEN every button, switch, … on a route is activated THEN <html> never gets data-theme'. Both current screens have no controls, so the loop runs 0 times and only adds an annotation. The real enforcement is src/app/theme-source.test.ts, regex `/data-theme|dataset\.theme|colorScheme|color-scheme/`, which scans only `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css}`. It does not scan index.html (e.g. `<meta name="color-scheme">`), and it misses a computed attribute name such as `setAttribute('data-' + key, …)`.
findings.suggestion: Fail, or at least log a visible warning, when `activated === 0` on a screen that is expected to have controls. Add index.html to the theme-source scan. Record in the spec or tasks that this scenario is enforced statically for this slice.

findings.title: Served-behind-one-origin scenarios are only checked as config text, never executed
findings.evidence: Scenarios 'API through the frontend origin' ('/api/child/nope … is the backend's 404 problem+json, with the security headers') and 'Missing asset' ('/assets/missing.js … 404, not the SPA page') are checked only by regex over nginx.conf. 'Image build without the contract' is checked only by comparing string positions in the Dockerfile. Task 4.4, the compose smoke, is unticked, and no `docker build` or curl run is recorded. The config itself looks right: variable `proxy_pass $backend` keeps the URI; `Host $http_host`; XFF is overwritten; server-level `add_header … always` with no add_header inside locations; `/assets/` uses `=404`; `/` uses `try_files $uri /index.html` plus `expires -1`.
findings.suggestion: Do task 4.4 and record the curl -i output for /api/child/nope, /assets/missing.js and /some/route as evidence. Add a scripted `docker build` with the contract removed (or a CI job) so the Dockerfile scenario is executed, not only matched as text.

findings.title: Real-name guard only reads body innerText
findings.evidence: Requirement (NFR-3): 'a page that shows the real one … SHALL fail the run'. `expectNoRealName` checks only `page.locator('body').innerText()`. The real name in `document.title`, `aria-label`, `alt`, `title` or an input value would pass the guard but still appear in recordings, screenshots or the accessibility tree. The fixture also skips the guard when `page.url() === 'about:blank'`, so setContent-based tests are never guarded.
findings.suggestion: Also check document.title, text attributes and input values (as `uiTexts` does in the unit test).

findings.title: Provenance check exempts contract/ and docs/qa recordings, which the spec does not document
findings.evidence: Spec: 'every image, font, audio, video, PDF, office or plain-text data file anywhere in the repository … SHALL be listed'. The code adds `OUT_OF_SCOPE = ['contract/']` and exempts docs/qa files that a recording manifest lists. fixtures/PROVENANCE.md mentions both exemptions, but the spec delta does not. The fixture and asset roots in the spec (fixtures/, e2e/fixtures/, evals/cases/, public/, src/assets/, src/design-system/fonts|icons/) are all covered.
findings.suggestion: Amend the spec delta to state the contract/ and recorded-evidence exemptions, so the spec and the check say the same thing.

findings.title: Lint rule scope leaves out src/test/** helpers and .js/.jsx files
findings.evidence: Spec: the lint rule refuses literal UI text 'in `src/`'. The config applies the rule to `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` and ignores `src/test/**` entirely, not only `*.test.*`. A non-test render helper or a .jsx component under src/ would not be linted.
findings.suggestion: Limit the ignore to `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` and `src/test/setup.ts`, and add `js,jsx` to the files glob (or forbid .js/.jsx under src/).

findings.title: nginx behaviour beyond the spec (scope drift)
findings.evidence: Implemented but not in the 'Served behind one origin' requirement: `client_max_body_size 51m`, `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme`, `proxy_hide_header` of the backend's security headers, and extra CSP directives (`style-src 'unsafe-inline'`, `img-src data: blob:`, `connect-src`, `form-action`). Separately, `/api` without a trailing slash falls through to the SPA instead of the backend.
findings.suggestion: Amend the spec delta to cover the upload body limit and header de-duplication, or move them to the slice that owns uploads (NFR-17). Decide whether `/api` should redirect or proxy.

findings.title: Task 2.1 description does not match the implemented pseudo-catalog
findings.evidence: Task 2.1: 'shows only `⟦`-prefixed text'. The spec scenario and the code (`COVERED` regex, i18n-coverage.test.tsx:17) use whole `⟦…⟧` segments, which is stricter. Tasks 2.8 (RED run) and 4.3 to 4.6 are correctly left unticked.
findings.suggestion: Update the task 2.1 text to 'whole ⟦…⟧ segments' to match the spec.

findings.title: Literal arguments to method calls slip past both NFR-9 layers (lint and pseudo-catalog)
findings.evidence: For a CallExpression with a MemberExpression callee, `literalTexts` only checks the receiver (`return literalTexts(node.callee.object)`), never the arguments. So `{t('greeting').replace('{name}', 'kamaráde')}`, `{t('a').concat(' bodů')}` and `{[t('a'), t('b')].join(' a ')}` are not reported. The pseudo-catalog backstop misses the first two as well. In i18n-coverage.test.tsx, `COVERED = /^(?:…⟦[^⟦⟧]*⟧)+…$/u` accepts any characters inside the brackets. Because `.replace`/`.concat` work on the wrapped string, the result is `⟦Ahoj kamaráde⟧` or `⟦…⟧ bodů`. The first matches COVERED. Lint and render test both pass while Czech literal text reaches the screen.
findings.suggestion: For method calls, also scan the arguments for literals (or at least the arguments of `replace`/`replaceAll`/`concat`/`join`/`padStart`/`padEnd`), and add the cases to lint-rule.test.ts. In the pseudo test, also check that the text inside each ⟦…⟧ segment equals a catalog value, so changing a catalog string after lookup is caught.

findings.title: Lint rule and pseudo test both skip `value` on text inputs and textareas
findings.evidence: `isTextAttribute` treats `value` as text only for `<input type=submit|button|reset>`. `<input value="Ahoj" readOnly />` and `<textarea value="Ahoj" />` show the literal on screen but are not reported (lint-rule.test.ts:24 even lists a text input with `value` as valid, though there it is an expression). `uiTexts` in i18n-coverage.test.tsx likewise reads `value` only for submit/button/reset inputs, so the render backstop does not see the text either. The pseudo test's TEXT_ATTRIBUTES also leaves out `aria-brailleroledescription`, which the lint rule does list.
findings.suggestion: Report literal `value` on `textarea` and on `input` elements that have no type or a text-like type (text, search, email, url, tel). Read `.value` of text inputs and textareas in `uiTexts`, and make TEXT_ATTRIBUTES match the rule's DOM_TEXT_ATTRIBUTES.

findings.title: Pseudo-catalog test only checks the first render of each route
findings.evidence: `renderSettled` mounts the app, waits one macrotask and reads the DOM. Error banners, dialogs, toasts, validation messages and loading/empty states driven by queries never render in this test. The comment on the lint rule (and spec line 33-34) call this test the backstop for text reached through a variable or another module, e.g. `const ERR = {x: 'Chyba'}` and `{ERR.x}`. That text bypasses both layers whenever it shows only after an interaction or an API response. No product screens exist in slice 1, so there is no impact yet, but the guarantee is weaker than the spec says.
findings.suggestion: Document the limit in the spec and design, or have feature slices register extra states (e.g. route + fixture/interaction factories) that the pseudo test also renders. At minimum, also forbid module-level string literals in feature folders, or flag object literals whose values have letters in `src/features/**` outside the i18n catalog.

findings.title: Theme source guard misses index.html and other ways to force a theme
findings.evidence: `sources('src')` scans only `.ts/.tsx/.css` under src/. A `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light">` in the root `index.html`, or a `class="dark"`, is not scanned. The regex `/data-theme|dataset\.theme|colorScheme|color-scheme/` also misses `setAttribute('data-' + 'theme', …)`, `classList.add(...)` and `style.setProperty('--paper', …)`. The test's docblock says it covers 'screens and states [the e2e] cannot reach', so these gaps are not covered anywhere.
findings.suggestion: Add `index.html` to the scanned files. Consider also flagging `setProperty('--paper'`/`--ink` and theme-like `classList` writes on `documentElement`/`body`.

findings.title: No-toggle e2e misses some control types and changes that land after its check
findings.evidence: CONTROLS has no `a[href]`, `summary`, `[role=tab]`, `[role=menuitem]`, `[role=option]` or `input[type=range]`. A theme switch built as a link, a details/summary disclosure or a tab would never be clicked, though the spec says 'every … menu toggle on a route is activated'. Also, right after each click `toHaveCount(0)` passes at once if the count is already 0. The finding holds, though the line number is off: the directive is at nginx.conf:14, not line 42. `client_max_body_size 51m;` is set once at the `server` level. - The attacker's own LAN upload speed limits how fast they can send.
- The threat model is a home LAN server. A device on that LAN could flood the box in many simpler ways.

rejected.title: nginx behaviour beyond the spec (scope drift)
rejected.evidence: Implemented but not in the 'Served behind one origin' requirement: `client_max_body_size 51m`, `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme`, `proxy_hide_header` of the backend's security headers, and extra CSP directives (`style-src 'unsafe-inline'`, `img-src data: blob:`, `connect-src`, `form-action`). Separately, `/api` without a trailing slash falls through to the SPA instead of the backend.
rejected.suggestion: Amend the spec delta to cover the upload body limit and header de-duplication, or move them to the slice that owns uploads (NFR-17). Decide whether `/api` should redirect or proxy.
verifierNotes:
The nginx config does not contradict the "Served behind one origin" requirement, and the rest of the change documents the extra behaviour the finding lists.

1. **The spec sets minimums, not an exact list.** It says the CSP must include `script-src 'self'`, `object-src 'none'` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`. Line 20 has all three. Adding `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`, `img-src data: blob:`, `connect-src` and `form-action` does not break that, and design.md explains `'unsafe-inline'` ("React `style` props need them (scripts stay `'self'`)").

2. **`client_max_body_size 51m` is documented.** design.md, in its Serving section, says "`client_max_body_size 51m` follows NFR-17's 50 MB upload cap", and the comment at nginx.conf line 13 says the same. Without it, nginx's default 1 MB limit would reject uploads that NFR-17 allows. So this is a recorded design decision that supports another requirement, not undocumented drift.

3. **`proxy_hide_header` is how the header requirement gets met.** The spec says every response, including proxied ones, must carry the security headers. Hiding the backend's copies stops them being sent twice, and design.md documents it: "the backend's copies of the server-level security headers are hidden".

4. **`X-Forwarded-Proto` is a standard, harmless proxy header.** The spec requires forwarding Host and the client address; adding one more forwarded header does not conflict with that.

5. **`/api` with no trailing slash is behaving as the spec says.** The spec says to proxy `/api/` (with the slash) and that "a path that is not a built file SHALL get the SPA". `/api` is not a built file, so serving the SPA there is the specified behaviour, not a bug. The contract client only calls paths under `/api/`.

None of these is a correctness defect. At most it is a documentation preference, and the design doc already covers most of it.

I checked nginx.conf against the change's spec.md (Requirement "Served behind one origin", lines 130-149) and design.md (lines 98-110). Nothing in the finding can actually happen to a user or an attacker, and most of the claimed drift is already covered by the change's own docs.

1. **`client_max_body_size 51m` and `proxy_hide_header`.** design.md lines 101 and 108-109 cover both. It says the 51m limit "follows NFR-17's 50 MB upload cap" and that "the backend's copies of the server-level security headers are hidden". The header hiding isn't extra behaviour. It is what makes the spec's rule work: "Every response SHALL carry X-Content-Type-Options…" should give one value per header, not two. nginx can't scope the body limit to one route ahead of time, and without it nginx's default 1 MB cap would block NFR-17's 50 MB uploads.

2. **The extra CSP directives.** The spec asks for a CSP "with script-src 'self', object-src 'none' and frame-ancestors 'none'". That sets a minimum, not a complete list. 3. **`/api` without a trailing slash going to the SPA.** This is what the spec asks for. It says to proxy `/api/` (with the slash), and that "A path that is not a built file SHALL get the SPA". The generated client only calls `/api/...` paths, so no real request reaches bare `/api`. If one did, it would just get the SPA shell, which is harmless.

4. **`X-Forwarded-Proto`.** This is the only directive the docs don't mention. It is a standard proxy header with no security or behaviour impact here, which is not enough to justify a finding.
